title: Cubist Nightmares in Comics
content: Newspaper comics came of age during the same time that modern art made its appearance, and the comic artists took notice.In 1916, just a few years after the Armory Show, Penny Ross portrays "a Cubist Nightmare in the Studio of Monsieur Paul Vincent Cezanne Van Gogen Ganguin."InPolly and Her Pals(1929) by Cliff Sterrett, Paw accidentally tries on his wife's glasses, with disorienting results.Uncle Walt and Skeezix visit an art museum and find out what it's like to walk around in Modernist paintings, as portrayed inGasoline Alley(1930) by Frank King.Bill Watterson continued the tradition decades later inCalvin and Hobbes.-----You can find these pages and more inThe Smithsonian Collection of Newspaper Comics
